title: Sorting-based Techniques, Comparators & Coordinate Compression (Depth)
relevance: High (sort-then-greedy, event order, and rank-compression + Fenwick still dominate harder OA / Div2 C–D array problems)
company_notes: Typed inventory / coupon assign (USB vs PS/2, discount tiers): sort price and fill constrained buckets first. Meeting rooms / k workers (Room Allocation, Movie Festival II): event sort plus reuse earliest-free resource. Leaderboard uniqueness / rank remap (Ratings Change, Best Price): sort preferences or thresholds, assign next free rank or evaluate at compressed candidates. Count inversions / range pairs under 1e9 values (Seating D2, Petya and Array, Deque optimization): compress then Fenwick, same family as count-smaller-to-the-right.

phases.goal: Spot depth sorting problems that hinge on the right sort key, event secondary order, or compressing every DS-touched index.

must_hit.point: After the famous ladder, the next skill is which key to sort on under constraints (ties, open/close events, free-item thresholds) and compressing every index the DS will touch (including r+1 removals / prefix values).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names sort-key choice under ties/events/thresholds and compressing every touched index, not just a plain sort-then-scan.

must_hit.point: Spot it when values are ≤1e9 but n≤2e5, when greediness needs a multiset over a sorted stream, or when a rewrite like a_i−b_i turns a pairwise condition into a 1D sorted scan.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites ≤1e9 with n≤2e5, sorted-stream+multiset greediness, or an a_i−b_i rewrite to a 1D scan.

must_hit.point: OA/interview skins include typed inventory/coupon assign, meeting rooms/k workers, leaderboard uniqueness/rank remap, and count inversions/range pairs under 1e9 values via compress-then-Fenwick.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps the prompt to one of those four skins from Where it appears.

probes: What tells you this is a depth sorting problem—sort-key/event order/compression—rather than a plain sort-then-scan template?
If values are ≤1e9 with n≤2e5, or greed needs a multiset over a sorted stream, or a pairwise inequality rewrites to a_i−b_i, what do you reach for?

hints.1: Ask whether the hard part is which key to sort on, how events tie-break, or which coordinates the DS will touch.
hints.2: Cue triad: ≤1e9 with n≤2e5; multiset over a sorted stream; rewrite like a_i−b_i to a 1D sorted scan.
hints.3: Say: pick the constrained sort key (ties/open-close/thresholds) and compress every DS index including r+1 removals/prefixes; skins are coupon buckets, k-resource reuse, rank remap, and compress+Fenwick pair counts.

phases.goal: Choose the right sort key, rewrite, event model, or sorted-stream+multiset before coding.

must_hit.point: Rewrite before sorting: inequalities like a_i+a_j>b_i+b_j map to sorting a−b (Pair of Topics); do not invent a 2D comparator.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rewrites the pairwise inequality to sort a−b (or a_i−b_i) and rejects a 2D cmp.

must_hit.point: Exchange argument ⇒ sort key: Tasks and Deadlines sorts by duration ascending (not deadline); Hanoi / nesting rings sorts outer radius descending with a careful inner tie-break.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States duration↑ for Tasks and Deadlines, or outer↓ with inner tie-break for nesting rings.

must_hit.point: Greedy over a sorted stream + multiset: Knights / Movie Festival II / Too Many Segments — sort the primary key, maintain a dynamic bag of active ends/loots, delete the extremal element when a constraint breaks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sorts primary key then maintains a multiset/bag and deletes the extremal element on constraint break.

must_hit.point: Suffix/prefix after one sort: Monster Killing (suffix max power), Air Conditioners (prefix/suffix min cost) — once positions are ordered, answers are linear scans.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Orders positions once, then answers with a suffix-max or prefix/suffix min linear scan.

must_hit.point: Movie Festival II: k attendees; sort by end and assign each film to the latest free end ≤ start. Too Many Segments: scan x, keep active segments by r, greedily delete furthest r when coverage >k.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes latest-free-end assignment for k attendees, or furthest-r deletion when coverage exceeds k.

probes: How do you turn a pairwise inequality into a 1D sort key instead of inventing a 2D comparator?
What exchange argument or sorted-stream+multiset template picks the sort key here?
After one positional sort, when is the rest just a prefix/suffix linear scan?

hints.1: Try a rewrite or exchange argument before designing a fancy comparator.
hints.2: Pair of Topics → a−b; Tasks/Deadlines → duration↑; Knights/Movie II/Too Many Segments → sorted stream + multiset; Monster Killing / Air Conditioners → suffix/prefix after sort.
hints.3: Say: rewrite a_i+a_j>b_i+b_j to sort a−b; exchange ⇒ duration↑ or outer↓+inner tie-break; maintain active ends/loots and drop the extremal; or finish with suffix-max / prefix-suffix mins.

phases.goal: Show strict-weak-order ties, event secondary keys, offline Fenwick ranking, and correct r+1 compression.

must_hit.point: Offline Fenwick template: collect every value that will be update/query’d (array values and derived prefixes) → sort+unique → lower_bound ranks → then scan.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Collects all update/query values including derived prefixes, sort+unique, lower_bound ranks, then scans.

must_hit.point: Compress the event you update, not a proxy: for range cover include r+1 (or r if inclusive ends are stored consistently) in the coordinate list — rank(r)+1 is a different wrong point when holes exist (Feed Cats).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Puts the removal coordinate r+1 into the coordinate list and rejects rank(r)+1 when holes exist.

must_hit.point: Strict weak order under ties (Correct Placement): sort by width ascending with height descending on ties so a same-width peer is not treated as already seen; then scan with running min height.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses width↑ and height↓ on ties, then a running-min-height scan.

must_hit.point: Event secondary key: decide open-vs-close order explicitly (+1 before −1 or the reverse); Room Allocation / Online games WA if a room frees after the same-time arrival is processed wrong. Online games emits +1 at A and −1 at A+B.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States an explicit +1/−1 secondary order at equal times and names the same-time free-after-arrival WA.

probes: Walk through the offline Fenwick rank pipeline when prefixes are also queried.
What coordinate do you compress for a range-cover removal, and why is rank(r)+1 wrong?
How do you break width ties in Correct Placement, and how do you order same-time open/close events?

hints.1: Think ranks for every touched value, removal coordinates, and explicit tie/event order.
hints.2: sort+unique+lower_bound on values and prefixes; compress r+1 not rank(r)+1; width↑ height↓; fix +1 vs −1 at equal times.
hints.3: Spell: collect update/query values and derived prefixes → sort+unique → lower_bound → scan; include r+1 in coords; Correct Placement width↑ height↓ then running min height; decide +1 before −1 (or reverse) so same-time free/arrival cannot WA.

phases.goal: Explain why huge values force compression at n≤2e5 and why one sort unlocks linear answer scans.

must_hit.point: When values are ≤1e9 but n≤2e5, Fenwick/segment structures must sit on compressed ranks of the values they touch, not on the raw value domain.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts ≤1e9 values with n≤2e5 and insists on rank compression before Fenwick/segtree indexing.

must_hit.point: Count inversions / range pairs under 1e9 values (Seating D2 / Petya and Array / Deque optimization) stay feasible by compressing then using Fenwick—same family as count smaller to the right.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names compress-then-Fenwick for 1e9-scale values instead of indexing the raw domain.

must_hit.point: Suffix/prefix after one sort: once positions are ordered, Monster Killing and Air Conditioners finish with linear scans (suffix max / prefix-suffix mins) rather than further heavy structure.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says one ordering pass then linear suffix-max or prefix/suffix min scans.

probes: Why do ≤1e9 values with n≤2e5 force coordinate compression before Fenwick?
How do inversion / prefix-pair counts under 1e9 values stay tractable?
After positions are sorted, what is left for Monster Killing or Air Conditioners?

hints.1: Separate the huge value domain from the n≤2e5 number of ranks you can afford.
hints.2: Compress every touched value/prefix, then Fenwick; or finish with linear prefix/suffix scans after one sort.
hints.3: Say: ≤1e9 with n≤2e5 ⇒ ranks then Fenwick (Seating/Petya/Deque); after one positional sort, answers are linear suffix-max or prefix/suffix mins.

phases.goal: Catch proxy compression, weak tie orders, missing rewrites, and same-time event ordering bugs.

must_hit.point: Using rank(r)+1 instead of compressing the removal coordinate r+1 — a different wrong point when holes exist.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects rank(r)+1 and requires r+1 (or consistent inclusive r) in the coordinate list.

must_hit.point: Sorting equal widths without height-descending order so a same-width peer is treated as already seen (Correct Placement).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Adds height↓ on equal widths so same-width peers are not marked already seen.

must_hit.point: Inventing a 2D comparator for a_i+a_j>b_i+b_j instead of rewriting to sort a−b (Pair of Topics).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Drops the 2D cmp and sorts a−b after the rewrite.

must_hit.point: Leaving open-vs-close secondary order unspecified so a room frees after the same-time arrival is processed wrong (Room Allocation / Online games).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Picks an explicit +1-before−1 or reverse secondary key at equal times.

must_hit.point: Sorting Tasks and Deadlines by deadline instead of duration ascending when the exchange argument says reward depends on durations.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Switches the key to duration ascending, not deadline.

probes: What goes wrong if you compress rank(r)+1 for a range-cover removal?
How can Correct Placement or Room Allocation WA from tie / same-time ordering?
Why is a 2D comparator the wrong first move on Pair of Topics, and why is deadline the wrong key on Tasks and Deadlines?

hints.1: Check proxy ranks, tie order, rewrite vs 2D cmp, and event secondary keys.
hints.2: Compress r+1; height↓ on equal widths; rewrite to a−b; decide +1 vs −1 at equal times; duration↑ not deadline.
hints.3: Also: Feed Cats needs the removal coordinate itself; same-width peers must not look already seen; Room Allocation/Online games WA on same-time free-after-arrival.

tradeoffs.topic: Compress removal coordinate r+1 vs rank(r)+1
tradeoffs.strong_answer: For range cover, include r+1 (or r if inclusive ends are stored consistently) in the coordinate list — rank(r)+1 is a different wrong point when holes exist (Feed Cats).

tradeoffs.topic: Rewrite to sort a−b vs inventing a 2D comparator
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Inequalities like a_i+a_j>b_i+b_j rewrite to sorting a−b (Pair of Topics); do not invent a 2D cmp.

tradeoffs.topic: Duration ascending vs deadline (Tasks and Deadlines)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Exchange argument ⇒ sort by duration ascending, not deadline; reward is independent of order except durations.

tradeoffs.topic: Open-before-close vs reverse at equal event times
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Decide open-vs-close order explicitly (+1 before −1 or the reverse); Room Allocation / Online games WA if a room frees after the same-time arrival is processed wrong.

tradeoffs.topic: Sorted stream + multiset vs plain sort-then-scan
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Knights / Movie Festival II / Too Many Segments need sort of the primary key plus a dynamic bag of active ends/loots, deleting the extremal element when a constraint breaks.

tradeoffs.topic: Outer radius descending with inner tie-break vs naive nesting order
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Hanoi / nesting rings: sort outer descending with a careful inner tie-break, then nest with a monotonic structure.

gotchas.trap: Compressing rank(r)+1 as a proxy for range-cover removal.
gotchas.correction: Compress the removal coordinate r+1 (or r if inclusive ends are consistent); rank(r)+1 is wrong when holes exist.

gotchas.trap: Equal widths ordered so a same-width peer looks already seen while scanning heights.
gotchas.correction: In Correct Placement, sort width ascending with height descending on ties, then scan with running min height.

gotchas.trap: Inventing a 2D comparator for pairwise a/b inequalities.
gotchas.correction: Rewrite a_i+a_j>b_i+b_j to sort a−b (Pair of Topics), then two-pointers / lower_bound.

gotchas.trap: Unspecified open/close secondary key at equal times.
gotchas.correction: Choose +1 before −1 or the reverse explicitly; otherwise Room Allocation / Online games can free a room after a same-time arrival is processed wrong.

gotchas.trap: Sorting Tasks and Deadlines by deadline.
gotchas.correction: Exchange argument ⇒ sort by duration ascending; reward depends on durations, not deadline order.

gotchas.trap: Forgetting derived prefixes when building Fenwick ranks.
gotchas.correction: Offline template: collect every update/query value including derived prefixes → sort+unique → lower_bound ranks → then scan.

gotchas.trap: Using only a plain sort when the greedy needs a live bag of ends/loots.
gotchas.correction: Sort the primary key and maintain a multiset of active ends/loots; delete the extremal element when the constraint breaks (Knights / Movie Festival II / Too Many Segments).
